blocking_issues: Rule 2 / phase block 'ground truth only through the sim writer path': D-182 sends a launched simulator's stdout to data/live_mode/sim/<n>.log, and step 2 / test_cli_live_mode say the simulator prints the actor (only 'not in its first line'). So every UI or live-check launch would write who flew it into a file under the app's data folder, outside data/truth.duckdb. Fix: print the actor and nickname only when stdout is an interactive terminal (or only behind a flag the API never passes). Write API-launched children's logs without them, or send that output to DEVNULL. Never log the child's argv, which carries --actor. Add a test that a launched child's log contains no actor id or nickname.

Rule 4 (every random draw comes from a seeded Generator derived from the global seed): D-177 takes the seed of a launch with no --seed from OS entropy. Derive it deterministically instead, for example rng_for(world_seed, 'live', 'seed', str(n)) with a launch counter n kept in clock.json, or stable_int of the world seed plus the reserved clock instant. Still print and record it. Successive launches keep their variety and the run stays reproducible. Add this to test_live_clock or test_sim_live.
suggestions: live_truth rows survive `live reset` (D-179). The block says reset removes 'all' live-generated rows, so either justify this explicitly in D-179 (the API may touch truth only through eval) or clear live_truth through sim/writers from the CLI `live reset` / `live check` cleanup when no API is running. Keep the live_truth DDL in sim/writers.py, not store/ddl.py, because the extended FORBIDDEN scan would flag ddl.py.

Sensor track ids are hashes of (seed, flight key, drone), so relaunching the same seed in one app session reuses ids, and D-174 opens a track only for an 'unseen' id. Salt the id with the launch instant, or treat an id whose track has closed as a new track. Add a hub test that relaunches the same seed.

If the feed goes silent (the simulator is killed or crashes), feed time stops and the incident never closes, so no Reveal button appears. Consider closing on simulator exit, or a wall-clock fallback. Bound FeedClient's reconnect so an orphaned child exits instead of retrying forever, and keep the child in the API's process group or have it check whether its parent died.

livemode.spec.ts: set test.setTimeout well above the 120 s default, since queued reruns at speed 20 on a slow container can take 1 to 2 minutes. Do the live reset and ledger reseed in afterAll/finally, so a failure cannot pollute the specs that run after it (pages, pages8, perf, screens, swarm).

Make sure LiveStreamMessage (and the ingest union) reach web/openapi.json through a schema route such as GET /api/schema/live-stream, as /api/schema/stream does, so types.gen.ts covers them. Add a contract test with one example of every live message type.

Web task details the plan does not state explicitly: the installation picker for the watched installation (for example defaulting to the launch base), the confirm dialog on Reset live data, and a 'Live incidents this session' list that survives a page reload (list the session's incidents in hello or status).
Serve learned live tracks from GET /api/history/{track_id} (and the lens) through the composite store. Otherwise the ghost trail of the new-operator-twice second flight's top match returns 404.

D-180 reads 'by T+120 s' as 'any rerun at or before T+120' for returning-prober but 'the latest rerun at or before T+120' for copycat. The stricter reading is fine, but say why in D-180, or align the two.

In DEMO.md's Live mode section, say to press R (reseed) before the replay demo after live use. Live ledger events stamped in September push recorded_at forward (D-010), so new replay proposals would fall after the Case board's as-of replay clock.
Say explicitly that test_live_hub feeds detections with a fake clock (no real-time waiting at 'speed 1'), so make check stays fast.
Minor accuracy: DuckTrackStore.over already exists in the working tree, and the existing Vitest file is web/tests/router.test.ts (not routes.test.ts; web tests live in web/tests/).
summary: A thorough plan that matches the code (the sim, match, live, store, memory and api functions it names exist with the expected shapes). Every task checkbox, test bullet and exit-check criterion is mapped to concrete files, tests and commands, including the soft live-check gate (D-063), the docs, and the phase docs and READMEs. Two easy-to-fix rule problems block approval: API-launched simulator logs would store the actor outside truth.duckdb (rule 2 and the block's 'only through the sim writer'), and default seeds come from OS entropy (rule 4). Everything else is a robustness or clarity suggestion.
